package_info.package_manager: N/A (proprietary software, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The vulnerability in PaperCut NG 22.0.5 allows unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary code as SYSTEM by abusing improper access control in the SetupCompleted class. The exploit enables attackers to set arbitrary authentication programs and inject malicious payloads, leading to full system compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Set auth program to C:\Windows\System32\ftp.exe (on Windows) or /usr/sbin/python3 (on Linux) via unauthenticated request.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During authentication, the code sets the authentication program to an attacker-controlled binary (ftp.exe or python3), allowing arbitrary command execution as SYSTEM.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Setting the authentication program to a system binary not intended for authentication is highly abnormal and enables arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, authentication programs are tightly controlled and not user-settable, especially not via unauthenticated requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would only involve trusted, pre-configured authentication binaries.
key_indicators: Ability to set authentication program via unauthenticated request
Use of system binaries (ftp.exe/python3) as authentication handlers

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: inputPassword contains logic to download a binary to C:\ProgramData\ and execute it (custom Go reverse shell).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During authentication, the code downloads a malicious binary (reverse shell) to C:\ProgramData\ and executes it, establishing a remote connection for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing a binary during authentication is highly abnormal and indicative of code execution abuse.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal authentication should only validate credentials, not perform network downloads or execute arbitrary binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download binaries, but never as part of authentication.
key_indicators: Network download of executable during authentication
Execution of attacker-supplied binary as SYSTEM

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Process tree: pc-app.exe -> ftp.exe -> cmd.exe -> AXtJxdUwlfJI.exe (reverse shell).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During authentication, the exploit spawns a process tree where the malicious payload is executed as a child of cmd.exe, itself a child of ftp.exe, avoiding direct parentage from pc-app.exe.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Manipulating the process tree to obscure the origin of the malicious process is a known anti-forensics technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal authentication does not spawn multiple processes or obfuscate process lineage.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may spawn subprocesses, but not in this context or with this intent.
key_indicators: Unusual process tree: authentication handler spawning ftp.exe/cmd.exe
Malicious payload not a direct child of main application

attack_chain.action: Attacker sets the authentication program to a system binary (ftp.exe or python3) via unauthenticated request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Allows arbitrary command execution during authentication.

attack_chain.action: Attacker initiates authentication with a crafted username and password, triggering the inputPassword logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binary is downloaded and executed as SYSTEM.

attack_chain.action: Malicious process is spawned via a manipulated process tree (pc-app.exe -> ftp.exe -> cmd.exe -> reverse shell), obscuring the attack's origin.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote SYSTEM-level access; attack is difficult to trace.

behavioral_signatures: Authentication handler setting arbitrary system binaries as authentication programs
Network downloads of executables during authentication
Process tree: pc-app.exe spawning ftp.exe/cmd.exe/unknown binaries
Absence of expected log entries for code execution events
file_indicators: Authentication configuration referencing ftp.exe or python3
network_indicators: Outbound connections from authentication process to external IPs/domains (reverse shell C2)
Unusual FTP or HTTP traffic during authentication events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for changes to authentication program configuration, especially referencing system binaries like ftp.exe or python3. Alert on network downloads and execution of new binaries during authentication. Analyze process trees for pc-app.exe spawning ftp.exe, cmd.exe, and unknown executables. Look for absence of expected log entries during authentication events. Flag unexpected binaries in C:\ProgramData\ and outbound connections from authentication processes.
